issue.title: Bug: Incorrect system time due to Chrony writing local time to RTC instead of UTC

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

**Issue Summary:**
On SONiC systems configured with a local timezone, the system time is incorrect due to a mismatch in how Chrony and the Linux kernel interpret the RTC (hardware clock) time.

**Background:**
By default, SONiC uses UTC for system operations. However, when the system timezone is set to a local time, Chrony misinterprets the intended format of the hardware RTC.

Linux expects the hardware RTC to always be in UTC.
Chrony, on the other hand, checks /etc/adjtime to determine whether the RTC should be in local time or UTC.

If /etc/adjtime is missing and rtconutc is not set, Chrony assumes the RTC is in local time,
As a result, Chrony writes local time into the RTC.

On reboot, Linux reads the RTC assuming it’s in UTC, and then applies the local timezone again.
This causes the system time to be offset by the timezone difference, effectively applying the offset twice.

Chrony fixes the incorrect system time by using a slewing mechanism, which could reach up to 200,000 ppm slewing rate for large offsets.
This affects processes/tests that rely on the system time.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Set the system timezone to the local time zone.
2. Reboot the device.
3. Observe the system time drift (e.g., off by UTC to local time zone diff).

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

Actual behavior - System time is offset from the actual time due to double timezone conversion.

Expected behavior - The system time should be accurate, regardless of the configured timezone.

### Relevant log output

```shell

Thu Apr 24 <IPV6> PM IDT 2025
sonic_user:~$
```

resolution.title: Tell chrony that the RTC is always in UTC
resolution.description:
Fixes #22437

#### Why I did it

Tell chrony that the RTC on devices is always stored in UTC and not the local time zone. For devices that are running on UTC, this won't change anything; for devices that are not running on UTC, this will correct some time issues where the kernel interprets the time in the RTC as being in UTC, but Chrony interprets that time as being in the local time zone.

##### Work item tracking
- Microsoft ADO **(number only)**: 33062976

#### How I did it

Add `rtconutc` to Chrony's configuration file.

#### How to verify it

Tested in community by setting a non-UTC timezone for the device and making sure that after a reboot, the time is set correctly.
